urn:eigenius:core:description: A named axiom: a closed term whose type the kernel admits without checking the term itself. The `axiom_statement` property carries an EigenTT type expression (typically inhabiting Prop) that the axiom is asserted to inhabit. Conversion treats the axiom IRI as opaque — never delta-unfolded. Voiding the layer that introduces an axiom removes it from the kernel environment for any chain resolution that excludes that layer. See D46 §10. An axiom is the *denotation* of the lexical entries whose `lexicon:sem` names it (a WordNet verb/adjective sense); its `core:description` carries that sense's natural-language gloss, so the concept-`core:description` text index (D63 lexicon-augmentation §6a index c) makes the gloss searchable for OOV grounding across all parts of speech.
The EigenTT type the axiom inhabits — typically a Prop. Encoded as a chain-mirrored EigenTT type expression per D47 (eigentt:Term).
Free-form note: why this axiom is being admitted, what trust assumption it encodes, what metatheory justifies it. For auditability — axioms are chain-traceable.

A named, chain-resident TRANSPARENT definition (D66). Unlike an `eigentt:Axiom`, whose IRI evaluates to a rigid neutral and never unfolds, a Definition names a body that decode substitutes at the use site. `definition_body` holds the body as a lambda chain `Lam(x1, T1, Lam(x2, T2, … B))`; arity and parameter types are read off `definition_type`, so nothing is stored twice. The body is stored ALREADY NORMALIZED — a definition's identity for equality and hashing is the normal form of its right-hand side (D66 D9), which is what lets a use decode to a normal term without evaluating. Recursive bodies are rejected at commit: decode would not terminate.

The declared type of the definition, e.g. `Set -> Set -> Set -> Prop`. Arity and parameter types are read from here rather than duplicated, so a stored arity can never contradict the type. D47-encoded (eigentt:Term).

The right-hand side as a lambda chain, stored in NORMAL FORM (D66 D9). Decode peels one leading `Lam` per supplied argument and substitutes, never forming a beta-redex, so a use decodes straight to a normal term. D47-encoded (eigentt:Term).

When true, decode does NOT unfold this definition: the IRI stays a rigid constant, like an axiom, and the definition's identity is the folded name rather than the normal form of its body (the D66 D9 carve-out). This is the strict-vs-unrestricted decode mode of issue #95. Absent means transparent.

A logic whose proof language the system HOSTS A CHECKER for. An inhabitant is a resource, not a bare tag, because admitting a logic is a governance act that carries evidence: which checker implementation, which comorphism, and the two arguments the design requires — soundness of the external turnstile against its satisfaction relation, and satisfaction-preservation by the comorphism. A nullary constructor could carry none of that. Adding a logic is therefore declaring a resource, which is also why this is a class rather than an inductive: the admissible set is the set of declared individuals, extended by a layer rather than by editing a type. Distinct from `prov:proof_system`, which records which verifier ran and is deliberately an open string — recording a verifier must not be a bootstrap edit, whereas admitting one to the trusted computing base must be. A logic with no hosted checker is not an inhabitant: it produces no judgement and cannot reach Verified.

The kernel's own type checker. The degenerate and privileged case: the type IS the proposition, so no comorphism is needed and the satisfaction-preservation obligation is vacuous. Under inhabitation semantics the assertion that the checker accepts `t : P` and the assertion that `P` holds are the same statement, so soundness is discharged by construction rather than argued.

Lean 4, re-checked in process by the `nanoda_lib` kernel reimplementation. Because that checker is statically linked into the host kernel, admitting this logic puts the whole of `nanoda_lib` inside the trusted computing base. Needs a comorphism relating the native Lean proposition to the graph proposition, and the primary risk it carries is not that the Lean kernel accepts falsehoods but that the translated proposition fails to denote the target one.

A CHECKED triple: a checker for `logic` verified `term` against `type`. This is the checkable unit, and the reification of justification logic's proof-checker operator — LP's positive-introspection axiom `t:F -> !t:(t:F)` names the evidence `!t` that `t` proves `F`, which is what a checker returns and what this constructor persists. An algebra carrying application and sum but no `!` runs the checker at commit time and discards the result; a judgement keeps it. It generalises the native `Ann(e, T)` annotation in the two ways annotation cannot serve: an annotation cannot name which logic's checker ran, and it is erased during evaluation, so it cannot be cited. Storage cost over an annotation is the logic tag alone, because an annotated term already carries its type inline. A slot ranging over this type is checked in CHECK mode — decode both fields, check `type` is a type, check `term` against it — so no slot relies on inference and no exemption list is needed.
